[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Buy second-hand first: Thrift stores, consignment shops, and online marketplaces like ThredUp or Poshmark.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Invest in quality over quantity: Choose timeless, well-made pieces.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Research eco-friendly brands: Brands like Patagonia, Everlane, and Reformation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Care for your clothes: Wash in cold water, line-dry or tumble dry on low.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Avoid fast fashion: Steer clear of brands that prioritize cheap, trendy items.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Rent or swap clothes: Consider clothing rental services or swapping with friends.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Upcycle or repurpose: Turn old t-shirts into reusable bags or create a quilt from worn-out jeans.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Support sustainable fabrics: Look for eco-friendly materials like organic cotton, recycled polyester, or Tencel.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Avoid microbeads and synthetic materials: Opt for natural fibers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Educate yourself: Follow sustainable fashion bloggers, influencers, or brands on social media.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tencel is a branded lyocell fiber produced by Lenzing AG from sustainably sourced eucalyptus trees.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Benefits of Tencel include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Sustainable sourcing from certified sustainable forests.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Low water usage in production.
